whyThisMatters: A password made from a name and a birth year can be guessed in seconds. Length, randomness, and mixed types are what slow an attacker. It is not personal cleverness.
policy: Synergy's password policy: 12+ characters, a mix of upper case, lower case, numbers and symbols, and NO personal information — no names, birth dates, months, or anything tied to who you are.
rememberThis: 12+ characters, mixed case, numbers, symbols, nothing personal — that's Synergy's policy, and now you've both spotted it and built it.

discussionPrompts: Ask the group to compare the password they built with how they make their own passwords. Is there anything that makes them think differently?
Ask why length matters more than adding one symbol. Can anyone explain it in their own words after watching the meter move?
Ask if anyone has reused a "strong" password on more than one account, and why that removes the strength.
For each Choose round, ask why the wrong options still "look" strong at a glance. What's the actual policy rule each one breaks?
facilitatorNotes.commonWrongAnswer: The most common mistake is stopping as soon as the meter turns green. People add just one symbol or number instead of making it longer. On the Choose rounds, people often pick the option with a symbol in it without checking length or personal info first.
